definitions.explanation: To run in various directions, typically with high energy, often used for children or animals.

definitions.gloss: to rush about, to run around busily
definitions.explanation: To be very busy running from place to place to get things done.

examples.japanese: {犬|いぬ}が{庭|にわ}を{走|はし}り{回|まわ}っている。
examples.english: The dog is running around the yard.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちは{元気|げんき}に{走|はし}り{回|まわ}っていた。
examples.english: The children were energetically running around.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}で{一日中|いちにちじゅう}{走|はし}り{回|まわ}っていた。
examples.english: I was running around all day for work.
examples.notes: [Note: Figurative use meaning to be very busy]

notes:
{走|はし}り{回|まわ}る is an intransitive verb ({自動詞|じどうし}) meaning to run around.

COMPOUND STRUCTURE:
- {走|はし}る (to run) + {回|まわ}る (to go around) → to run around

ASPECT (ている):
{走|はし}り{回|まわ}っている indicates an ongoing action of running around, often with energy.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {元気|げんき}に{走|はし}り{回|まわ}る (run around energetically)
- あちこち{走|はし}り{回|まわ}る (run around everywhere)
- {忙|いそが}しく{走|はし}り{回|まわ}る (run around busily)

USAGE NOTE:
Often used for children playing or animals being active. Also used figuratively to describe being very busy and having to go to many places.

[Register: Neutral]
